subject: Offboard proxy egress handshake and IP assertion for OnPrem rollout
messages:
From: Jane Doe <networkops@xpo.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: OnPrem rollout - egress IPs and proxy handoff

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we start the OnPrem rollout and begin decommissioning the legacy forward proxy, networking asked me to capture our constraints so your team can supply the static identifiers we need to allow from our perimeter. Key asks: 

- We need a definitive list of outbound IPs (or a small CIDR list) that the Private Endpoint(s) will originate from during normal operation and during the 2-week offboard overlap window.
- Is the control plane traffic to redwood-controlplane.redwood.ai over TLS only (443)? Any special SNI we should expect?
- Will you support mTLS between the customer gateway and the control plane, or will mutual auth be handled at the app layer?
- Any DNS hosts we should permit (FQDNs) in addition to IPs?
- Attachments: Im including our current egress allowlist (xpo-current-egress.csv). 

Goal: get a short-form assertion we can drop into our firewall change ticket and close the offboard loop. Can you get the list and a one-paragraph operational note by EOD Tuesday?

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Network Operations Manager, XPO Logistics

Attachment: xpo-current-egress.csv (stub)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <networkops@xpo.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: OnPrem rollout - egress IPs and proxy handoff

Hi Jane,

Appreciate the clear list. We can provide a short, signed IP assertion and an operations note for your firewall change. Preliminary answers inline: 

- Static outbound footprint: we will publish a small set of NAT IPs for the Private Endpoint; typically 2 active IPs (primary + standby) per region with an optional additional /29 for burst/maintenance. I will send the concrete CSV once we finalize allocation this afternoon.
- Control plane: TLS over 443; SNI is typically controlplane.redwood.ai for control-plane calls, and streaming endpoints use streaming.redwood.ai. We recommend allowing the base FQDNs rather than IPs for long-term rules, but understand firewall teams prefer IPs for emergency rules.
- mTLS: We do not require mTLS for the control plane for most private deployments; we support TLS with client cert pinning as an option for high-security customers. If XPO needs mTLS, we can enable a mutual-auth path and provide cert provisioning steps.
- DNS: We will provide a short list of FQDNs (controlplane, streaming, metrics ingestion) in the assertion document.

Next steps: Rishi will produce the official IP assertion file and operational blurb. Ben, can you coordinate the marketplace/procurement side for the offboard addendum (SOW changes) if needed?

Stephanie Nguyen
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-egress-assertion-template.csv (internal stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-10T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Offboard proxy egress handshake and IP assertion for OnPrem rollout

Stephanie / Rishi — quick note from the field: XPO's security team prefers a short overlap window (10 business days) and will want the assertion to include a rollback play if we see telemetry anomalies. Recommend we: 

1) Provide IP list + CSV for their firewall change ticket.
2) Add a one-paragraph rollback/runbook blurb (how to flip routing back to legacy proxy).
3) Include a retention note: what logs we will provide and for how long to support post-migration audit.

I can draft the sales-engineering blurb for the SOW addendum; Ben can handle procurement wording.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <networkops@xpo.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-11T15:46:00-07:00
Subject: IP assertion and operational handoff — XPO OnPrem private endpoints

Jane / XPO network team,

Following up with the formal assertion and handoff materials for the Private Endpoint offboard window. Please find the attached CSV that lists the static NAT IPs we will originate from during normal operation and during the two-week overlap: redwood-egress-ip-assertion-v1.csv. Summary below (copyable into your firewall ticket):

- Source: Redwood Private Endpoint (XPO-specific pool)
- Public NAT IPs (2026-08-11 deployment): 52.26.143.18, 52.26.143.19 (primary/standby)
- Emergency additional block: 52.26.143.16/29 (for maintenance failover)
- Ports/protocols: TCP 443 (control plane + streaming), outbound TCP 443 for metrics ingestion, and TCP 853 for DNS over TLS if DNS TLS is used. No inbound ports required to the origin.
- FQDNs to allow (recommended long-term rules): controlplane.redwood.ai, streaming.redwood.ai, metrics.redwood.ai
- mTLS: Not enabled by default. If XPO requires mTLS for control plane, we will enable it and provide certs; timeline for provisioning is ~3 business days.
- Rollback play: revert NAT to legacy proxy IPs in your ticket and hold new rules for 1 hour while we validate telemetry. If anomalies persist, open a priority incident to our on-call (see Drive link).
- Logs: We will provide 30 days of connection logs for the new pool and a 90-day retention option via Redwood Optimize add-on (see SOW addendum).

Attachments: redwood-egress-ip-assertion-v1.csv (static IP list), sow-offboard-addendum.pdf (procurement wording)

Please confirm receipt and I will tag this into the change ticket (CHG-124567) and push the Drive folder link.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
